Appearance:
 Shri Jahangir M. Poonegar - Advocate for the appellan
 Ms. Ayushi Thakur - Advocate appearing on behalf of S
 Parmar - Advocate for the respondent No.2.
 Shri Manoj Kumar Soni - Advocate for the respondent N
 Order

This present appeal under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicle Act, 1988 has been filed against the award dated 30.06.2016, passed in Claim Case No.14/2015 by Ist Additional Member MACT,
Khargone.
By the said award, learned Tribunal has granted compensation to the tune of Rs.1,30,000/- along with the interest of 6% per annum.

2. Factual matrix of the case are that on 04.01.2014 at around 4:00 pm, claimant met with an accident due to rash and negligent driving of respondent No.1 resulting into grievous injuries including fracture in the Tibia and Febula bone of right leg causing 20% permanent disability.
On account of such accident, a claim case was preferred by the claimant.
The Tribunal has considered that accident occurred due to rash and negligent NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-IND:3435 2 MA-2237-2016 driving of respondent No.1.
The offending vehicle is owned by respondent No.2 and insured with respondent No.3 on the fateful day.
After examining the evidence, the Tribunal awarded the compensation as noted above.

3. Learned counsel for the appellant submits that Tribunal has erred in calculating the award on the lower side and has not properly appreciated the fact that the doctor has issued 20% permanent disability certificate.
Tribunal has also wrongly assessed the lumpsum of Rs.75,000/- in the head of permanent disability.
He further argued thath, the learned Tribunal has also erred in calculating the compensation in the head of pain and suffering, attendant, special diet and transportation.
Counsel for the appellant submits that it is a very good case for enhancement of the compensation passed by the Tribunal.

4. Per contra, learned counsel for the respondent/Insurance company has supported the impugned award and submitted that learned Tribunal has rightly awarded the amount of compensation to the claimant, while considering the injuries sustained by the injured due to the accident.
He further argued that Tribunal has properly assessed the awarded amount in the different heads.
5. I have heard the rival submissions of learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
6. It is not in dispute that respondent No.1 was responsible for the offence and offending vehicle was insured with respondent No.3/Insurance company on the fateful day.

The only question for determination in this appeal is as to whether the amount awarded by the Claim's Tribunal requires NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-IND:3435 3 MA-2237-2016 any modification or not ?
7.

Therefore, applying the law laid-down by Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi reported in (2017) 4 ACJ 270 a n d Sarla Verma &
Others Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation & Others reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121 and considering the income of claimant as Rs. 4545/- per month as per Minimum Wages Act, future prospect 40%,
multiplier of 17 and permanent disability as 8% , the claimant is entitled to get the compensation as under:-
Head of permanent disability : Rs.01,03,844/-
 Pain and suffering : Rs.50,000/-
 Attendant : Rs.5,000/-
 special diet : Rs.5,000/-
 Transportation : Rs.5,000/-

Total Compensation : Rs.1,93,844/-
8.

Accordingly, this Court is of the considered opinion that the impugned award passed by the learned Tribunal warrant interference, the appellant is entitled to an enhancement for a sum of Rs.63,844/- (1,93,844 - 1,30,000).
The enhanced amount shall carry same interest as has been awarded by the Claims Tribunal.
Rest of the conditions, as imposed by the learned Claims Tribunal shall remain intact.

9. Further in view of the settled legal position of law, the insurance company is directed to indemnify the claimant at first instance, thereafter, they may recover the amount from owner and driver in accordance with law.

In view of the above, the appeal is partly allowed to the extent indicated herein above subject to following conditions:-

However, the compensation may be recovered from the driver and owner of the offending vehicle under the principle of 'pay and recover' ii.
The claimant is directed to pay the requisite Court Fee, if required in the present case.
iii. On such deposit, the claimant is permitted to withdraw the amount with accrued interest and costs, by filing a proper application before the Tribunal.
iv. The record be sent back to the learned Tribunal within three weeks from this day.
v. As a sequel, interlocutory applications pending consideration, if any, shall stand closed.
vi. No order as to costs.
